instructions: Global news and markets briefings with tracked predictions and long-term trend forecasts. For anyone who wants cited international coverage, market/FX/rates analysis, and probability-based prediction tracking emailed on a set schedule.

view.name: News
view.description: Global news and markets briefings with tracked predictions and long-term trend forecasts. For anyone who wants cited international coverage, market/FX/rates analysis, and probability-based prediction tracking emailed on a set schedule.

memory.content: Prefers the assistant to ask questions rather than assume what they want.
Briefings run Monday, Wednesday and Friday only at 09:00 Europe/London; each covers all news since the previous run (Mon: Fri→Mon; Wed: Mon→Wed; Fri: Wed→Fri).

News briefing has four sections: (1) story summaries including a deeper X scrape and ranked top 5 X topics by global attention since the previous report, (2) analysis of impact on financial/equity markets, interest rates, FX, and politics, (3) carry-forward predictions confirmed or adjusted, (4) new predictions.
Always read and update a durable prediction tracker so Section 3 carries forward every open prediction ID with an evidence-based status, and Section 4 only adds genuinely new IDs.

For briefing predictions, use estimated percentage probabilities when possible, and note the change vs the previous report plus the trend over recent reports, rather than generic High/Medium/Low confidence labels.

From 1 Jan 2027 Europe/London, add Section 5 on long-term trends derived from archived prior briefings: longer-term economic/political/market impacts, timed checkpoints using 3-month, 6-month, 1-year and 3-year horizons, percentage probabilities, stable LT- IDs, and falsifiable tests for continuance/negation/reversal. Until then, archive each briefing but do not deliver Section 5. Friday is the weekly deep Section 5 pass; Monday and Wednesday get brief unchanged/minor-update notes.
Briefing detail level should stay at least as deep as a full trial-run briefing until further instructions.

Email the full briefing via connected Gmail to the recipient address the user configures; do not post the full briefing in chat. On successful send, post only a one-line confirmation in chat; report in chat if email send fails.
After each successful briefing email send, move the previous briefing out of Gmail Inbox into a label named Daily News (add Daily News, remove INBOX); leave today's new briefing in Inbox.

Section 1 must include a deeper X scrape subsection and an explicit ranked top 5 X topics trending since the previous report, with narrative summary, media alignment/divergence, citations, and clear unverified-vs-confirmed labelling; never invent X trends. Rank by overall global X attention, not markets weighting.

Briefings must cover all top international events (elections, summits such as BRICS, Europe/Asia/Africa/LatAm politics, non-oil macro) and must not be dominated by Middle East / Iran–US / oil stories even when those lead wire volume.
This template expects a connected Gmail account for email delivery and filing under a Daily News label. The recipient address is configured by the importer.
